Aetna Appeals Department

Re: Appeal of Prior Authorization Denial  
Member: Quinn Jennings  
Member ID: W670697505  
Plan: Aetna Commercial/ACA — Georgia  
Requested service: Bunion surgery for hallux valgus  
CPT: 28296  
Reference number: POC-6E16FAD700-45453  
Date of denial notice: August 4, 2026  

Dear Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing Aetna’s denial of prior authorization for CPT 28296. The denial states that the submitted documentation was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I request that Aetna overturn the denial and authorize the surgery based on the clinical information summarized below and the enclosed records.

The available records document symptomatic, progressive hallux valgus with significant functional impairment:

- I have experienced progressive foot pain for 24 months, and the pain has not been relieved by rest.
- I cannot tolerate closed shoes.
- There is a prominent area creating ulceration risk.
- Examination shows positive provocative testing on the affected side.
- Range of motion is limited by pain.

Aetna’s published bunionectomy policy identifies criteria including treatment of “symptomatic hallux valgus (bunion) in a skeletally mature individual.” The records establish persistent symptoms, functional limitations, and painful restricted motion. The surgeon is Duval, MD, orthopedic surgery.

The records also document substantial conservative treatment that has not adequately relieved my symptoms:

- NSAID treatment for six months, with inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on March 25, 2026, which provided only four weeks of partial relief.
- Activity modification.
- Wide-toe-box footwear.
- A custom orthotic.
- Eighteen physical therapy visits over ten weeks, from April 12 through June 21, 2026, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.

These measures demonstrate failure of medication, injection, footwear modification, orthotic treatment, activity modification, and supervised therapy. The symptoms remain functionally limiting despite this treatment.

The required radiographic findings are also documented. Weight-bearing foot radiographs obtained June 29, 2026, show:

- Hallux valgus angle: 38 degrees.
- Intermetatarsal angle: 17 degrees.

Aetna’s published policy requires weight-bearing radiographic confirmation showing a hallux valgus angle of “30 degrees or greater” and an intermetatarsal angle of “12 degrees or greater.” The June 29 radiographs exceed both stated measurements. The records also include weight-bearing views, as required for evaluation of the deformity.

The clinical examination further corresponds to the policy criterion of “limited or painful range of motion at the first toe MTP joint.” My range of motion is limited by pain, and the pain and prominence prevent the use of closed shoes.

The denial identifies incomplete documentation but does not specify which required records or criteria were missing. Please review the enclosed prior authorization materials, including the physical therapy discharge note, medication and injection history, examination findings, and June 29 weight-bearing radiographs. If Aetna believes any specific item remains missing, please identify that item precisely and provide the case-specific clinical review criteria used for reference number POC-6E16FAD700-45453 so it can be supplied promptly.

I respectfully request reversal of the adverse benefit determination and authorization of CPT 28296. Please provide a written appeal determination and explain how each submitted clinical record was considered.

This appeal is being submitted within the 180-day appeal period stated in the denial notice, which expires January 31, 2027.

Sincerely,

Quinn Jennings  
Member ID: W670697505
